test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What happens to a stone tied to a string and moving in a circular path when the string is suddenly released?

options.text: It returns to its starting point
It changes direction and moves in a zig-zag path
It continues moving in the direction it was heading at the moment of release

solution:
The correct answer is __**It continues moving in the direction it was heading at the moment of release**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a stone tied to a string is whirled in a circular path, its **direction of motion** changes continuously at every point along the circle.
 
• The **velocity** of the stone at any point is always directed **tangent** to the circular path at that specific point.
 
• To keep the stone in this circular motion, a **centripetal force** is required, which is provided by the **tension** in the string directed toward the center of the circle.
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion** (the **Law of Inertia**), an object will continue to move in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an external force.
